definition: DialogOS is a graphical programming environment to design computer system which can converse through voice with the user.
details: Dialogs are clicked together in a Flowchart. DialogOS includes bindings to control Lego Mindstorms robots by voice and has bindings to SQL databases, as well as a generic plugin architecture to integrate with other types of backends. DialogOS is used in computer science courses in schools and universities to teach programming and to introduce beginners in the basic principles of human/computer interaction and dialog design. It has also been used in research systems. DialogOS was initially developed commercially by CLT Sprachtechnologie GmbH until its liquidation in 2017. The rights were then acquired by Saarland University and the software was released as open-source.

explainer.lead: DialogOS is a graphical environment for building systems that hold spoken conversations with people. Instead of writing all the dialogue logic as text, users assemble it as a flowchart and can connect it to robots, databases, and other backends.

tiers.eli5: DialogOS is like drawing a choose-your-own-adventure map for a talking computer. You connect boxes to decide what happens during a conversation. The finished system can talk with someone and even control a Lego robot.
tiers.practitioner: Use DialogOS to assemble voice-dialogue behaviour in a flowchart rather than conventional text-only code. Its bindings cover Lego Mindstorms and SQL databases, while the generic plugin architecture supports other backends. Keep backend integration and conversation design distinct when extending a system with plugins.
tiers.paperLevel: DialogOS represents a spoken-dialogue system as a graphically constructed flowchart, with external actions mediated by backend bindings or generic plugins. Supported integrations include Lego Mindstorms and SQL databases. Initially developed commercially by CLT Sprachtechnologie GmbH, it became open-source after Saarland University acquired the rights following the company's liquidation in 2017.

explainer.example: A student builds a flowchart for a voice-controlled Lego Mindstorms robot. The user speaks to the finished system, and the dialogue flow invokes the Mindstorms binding to control the robot.

explainer.intuition: A conversation can be planned like a map: each part of the flowchart represents a step, and the connections determine how the dialogue proceeds. DialogOS turns that visual plan into a voice-based system that can also communicate with external software or devices.
howItWorks: Create the dialogue by clicking its parts together in a flowchart.
Use the flowchart to define how the system converses with the user by voice.
Connect external actions through built-in bindings or plugins.
Control Lego Mindstorms robots, access SQL databases, or integrate another backend.
explainer.whyItMatters: It lowers the barrier to experimenting with spoken interaction by making dialogue structure visible and editable. The same environment supports teaching, introductory human-computer interaction, backend integration, and research prototypes.
misconceptions: It is not only a robot controller; voice-controlled Mindstorms is one available integration.
It is not limited to fixed built-in backends because its plugin architecture supports additional integrations.
It is no longer solely commercial software; Saarland University acquired the rights and released it as open-source.
